transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m not trying to make a big thing out of it, but I guess I’m here because of something that’s been going on at work for over a year now. I’m in computer support, and there’s this new ticket rotation and these security audits, and… it really seems like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me.

Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and maybe that’s what they want it to look like, I don’t know. I just feel like nobody is really taking it seriously when I try to explain it. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like people at work are intentionally trying to harm or undermine you, even if there's no clear evidence to support that belief?

I mean… “harm” sounds a little strong, and I don’t want to accuse anyone unfairly. But yes, I do feel like there are people at work who are trying to undermine me, or at least set things up so it looks like I’m not doing my job properly.

It’s been over a year with this new ticket rotation and the security audits, and it just feels like they’re building a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, so I know maybe it sounds like I’m overreacting… but that’s what it feels like to me.
Do you find yourself mistrusting people in general, or feeling like others are often out to get you, even outside of work?

I don’t think so… not in general, anyway. I mean, I try to be careful with people, but I wouldn’t say I walk around thinking everyone is out to get me.

It’s mostly this work situation that’s been hard to shake. Outside of that, I haven’t really noticed the same thing. Does that sound… I mean, that’s probably the best way to put it.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like people are acting against you or manipulating things in ways that aren’t obvious to others?

Not really outside of work, no… or at least, I don’t think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m seeing this everywhere.

It’s mainly the situation at work that I can’t get past. For over a year now, with the ticket rotation and the security audits, it feels like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying… I just don’t feel like anyone is taking seriously what it looks like from my side. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you believe that the things happening at work with the ticket rotation and security audits are being done specifically to target you, in a way that others don’t seem to notice or understand?

Yes… I mean, I’m trying not to make it sound dramatic, but that is why I’m here. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits aren’t just neutral policy changes.

It feels like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me specifically, even though management keeps showing me logs and saying, “This is just how it works.” I understand that’s what they’re saying, but from my side it feels targeted, and it seems like other people either don’t see it or don’t want to acknowledge it. Does that make sense?

Even though management has shown you logs and explained that these are standard policies, do you still feel certain that they are specifically targeting you and that the real reason is being hidden from you?

Yes… I mean, I know how that sounds, and I don’t want to seem like I’m refusing to listen. They have shown me logs, and they keep saying it’s just standard policy.

But I’m here because, for over a year now, I haven’t been able to shake the feeling that the ticket rotation and security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me specifically. Maybe I can’t prove the hidden reason in the way they want me to, but from my side it still feels like that’s what’s happening.

I’m trying to explain it fairly… does that make sense?

Even though you’ve seen the logs and management has explained that these are standard policies, do you still believe—deep down—that these actions are specifically targeted at you in a way that others don’t seem to recognize?

Yes… deep down, yes. I’m trying to be fair about it, because I know they’ve shown me the logs and they keep saying it’s just policy.

But I’m here because for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to understand that the ticket rotation and the security audits feel like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me at work. I know other people don’t seem to see it that way, or they think I’m reading too much into it, but from my side it still feels specifically aimed at me.

I hope I’m explaining that clearly.

Have you ever had any other experiences, either at work or elsewhere, where you felt things were being manipulated in a way that others don’t seem to notice—things that might sound unusual or hard to explain to someone else?

I don’t know if I’d say “elsewhere,” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

The main thing is really work. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits feel like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying… but it still doesn’t feel neutral to me.

I know that may sound hard to explain. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just can’t get past the sense that something is being arranged there that other people aren’t noticing. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever had any beliefs or concerns outside of work that other people find hard to believe or understand, even if you can’t quite explain them fully?

Not really outside of work, no… at least not in the same way. I don’t want to make it sound like I think everything is connected or anything like that.

It’s mainly this work situation. For more than a year I’ve been trying to get someone to understand that the new ticket rotation and the security audits feel like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. I know management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I hear that… I really do.

But I still can’t quite shake the concern that there’s more to it than they’re admitting. I know that may be hard for other people to understand. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you ever had any beliefs or concerns in life that you know other people might find strange or hard to believe, even if you yourself are sure they’re true?

I suppose… yes, there is the work situation, if that counts. I don’t want to make it sound strange or dramatic, because I know they keep telling me there’s an explanation for it.

But for over a year I’ve felt pretty sure that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build some kind of paper trail against me. Management has shown me logs and said it’s just standard policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying. I’m not trying to be unreasonable.

It’s just… I still believe there’s something targeted about it. Other people don’t seem to see it, so I know it may sound hard to believe. But to me it feels true. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had any beliefs or concerns — even ones you may not talk about much — that you know are hard for other people to believe or understand, even when you try to explain them?

Yes… I think the work thing is probably what I’d have to say. I don’t usually talk about it much because I know how it can sound, and I’m not trying to make anyone think I’m being difficult.

But I’m here because for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s their explanation.

I just… I don’t fully believe that’s all it is. And I know other people seem to have a hard time understanding why I’m concerned. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that you know are unusual and that you keep to yourself because you’re sure others wouldn’t understand them, even outside of work?

Outside of work… not really, no. I mean, I keep the work concerns to myself a lot because I know people don’t seem to understand it, and I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing anyone unfairly.

But it’s mainly that same situation I’ve mentioned — for over a year I’ve felt like the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me, even though management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy. I know that probably sounds unusual. I’m trying to answer you honestly without making it sound worse than it is.
Are there times when you feel like people are working against you or planning something, even when there's no proof, and even if it's not at work?

Not really outside of work… at least, I don’t think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m suspicious of everyone or anything like that.

It’s mainly the work situation I’ve been trying to explain. For over a year I’ve felt like the ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. I know management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just standard policy, and I understand that’s what they’re telling me.

I just haven’t been able to shake the feeling that it’s aimed at me. But no, I wouldn’t say I feel that way in every part of my life. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
